text:
julia: FYI ran a full 8xA100 throughput/tail run after the kernel-selector change landed. Seeing 2x tail latency on 4k-context workloads. Not a steady throughput drop, mostly tail spikes during steady state (30-90s into the run).

amir: ugh. which change? the heuristic that picks int8 kernels by seq_len distribution?

julia: yes — selector now prefers a quantized kernel variant for blocks when avg_seq_len < 256. But our real traffic has bimodal seqs so it picks wrong and we see repeated memcpy+recompile paths. attached nsys capture shows lots of tiny memcpy kernels and host-device syncs interleaved with NCCL ops.

ryan: can you share the nsys command you used? I'll try to reproduce in CI.

julia: ran: 
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --capture-range cudaProfilerApi --sample=none --trace=cuda,nvtx,nvtxu --force-overwrite --stats=true --duration=120 --cpucmd ./serve_bench --args "--model m1 --batcher config.json"
```
capture uploaded to perf storage: s3://redwood-perf/julia/2277771234.nsys

perf-bot: regression-alert: tail-latency jump detected for job=tp-8x-a100 on channel=canary. Suspected commit: 0a1b2c3 (kernel-selector heuristic) :bell:

amir: quick look: the timeline shows repeated short kernels on 1 stream then an NCCL allreduce on a different stream that waits ~1-2ms. That pattern kills overlap. It looks like the kernel selector launched per-layer small kernels on stream 0 without proper stream ordering / using different streams which starves the collective.

julia: here's an excerpt from nsys timeline (ascii):
```
[  20345ms ] kernelA_small (stream 0) 0.08ms
[  20345ms ] memcpy H2D small 0.04ms
[  20345ms ] kernelB_small (stream 0) 0.06ms
[  20346ms ] ncclAllReduce (stream 1) 1.9ms WAITING (depends on stream 0)
[  20348ms ] kernelC_small (stream 0) 0.07ms
[  20349ms ] ncclAllReduce (stream 1) 2.1ms WAITING
```
You can see the collectives would overlap if kernels were on different streams or if we batched those small kernels.

ryan: related: our batching heuristic currently groups by request arrival window only, not by seq_len buckets. If we bucket by seq_len and coalesce small ops into a single larger kernel call, we might reduce the number of tiny kernels and hence allow NCCL to overlap better.

amir: also worth checking the KV cache handshake. I saw in the trace a 2-3ms host-side RPC on the cache path right before the stalled NCCL; that could be forcing stream sync (we have a stream-synchronizing memcpy after cache hits).

julia: confirm — stacktrace from the server log around the pause: 
```
[20344.998] kv_cache: lookup(key=abc) -> hit
[20345.001] kv_cache: handshake wait 2.4ms (rpc rpc_id=4521)
[20345.004] launch kernel on stream 0
[20345.005] schedule nccl on stream 1
```
Looks like handshake delay + immediate small kernels = starvation.

amir: quick experiments: try two things locally — 1) disable the new selector (revert to baseline) and 2) change batcher to bucket by seq_len. Which is faster to test?

julia: I reverted selector locally, tail improved ~20% but still worse than baseline before the commit (so selector is part of it, not the whole story). I then tried seq_len bucketing in the batcher (coalesce small requests up to 512 tokens) — tail improved another ~15% and NCCL overlap looks normal in a short run.

ryan: nice. do you have the minimal patch for the batcher? we should ship that as a hotfix while we debug selector.

julia: pushed a WIP patch to canary: branch tp-bucket-batcher. Patch sets batcher.max_coalesced_tokens=512 and groups by floor(seq_len/64) bucket. Quick perf numbers in canary: p50 ~ unchanged, p95 down 18%, p99 down 26%.

perf-bot: perf-summary: before= p99 142ms, after-batcher= p99 105ms (canary), commit=tp-bucket-batcher.

amir: good mitigation. For the selector itself I want to add a cost model check: if selecting quantized kernel causes >N extra memcpy/kernel launches per layer (estimated from size + seq distribution) then prefer fallback. Also ensure kernel launches use per-layer multiple streams with correct events so NCCL can start earlier.

julia: agree. also need to fix KV handshake path to be non-blocking: don't do stream-synchronizing memcpy after handshake; instead stage data on pinned buffer and enqueue memcpy+kernel together.

sre-bot: reminder: schedule a reproducible perf run on the hw farm with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVLS and capture both nsys and nccl-profiling. Ticket: PERF-4621.

julia: plan: (1) land tp-bucket-batcher hotfix (canary -> prod gate), (2) instrument selector with a micro-cost estimator and revert toggle, (3) make KV handshake non-blocking in a follow-up. I'll attach nvprof and nccl logs to PERF-4621 and assign to @amir.

amir: I'll take the ticket. next steps: reproduce with the farm, then iterate on selector cost heuristic + kernel stream affinity.

ryan: thanks — I'll schedule the CI run and try to create a smaller unit test that exercises the seq_len bimodal case so this doesn't regress again.

julia: thanks team. I'll post updated traces to the ticket once the hotfix finishes canary (should be ~1 hour). :rocket:
